yarn-dinkum.meaning: Everything is kept: figures, dates, timestamps, links, the CCA rules and the notices. "make sniping harder" fairly renders mitigate; "Nobody can tell you what market prices will do down the track."
yarn-dinkum.sense: Terms fit: "people who had a go in the auction", "four lots", "That first auction's done and dusted", "still up for grabs in the final period", "before they had a crack at it".
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Sounds like an Australian writing the FAQ: "Auction 2 wrapped up just before general FOLD transferability was switched on.", "Have a read of the full [FOLD Auction Terms]".
yarn-dinkum.register: A light-to-moderate level 3 that leaves the notices formal: "had a go", "done and dusted", "up for grabs", "down the track", "had a crack at it". Perhaps a touch light.
yarn-dinkum.tone: The careful, clear FAQ tone holds; warnings stay serious: "Interfold team members and moderators will never ask for your seed phrase".
yarn-dinkum.flow: Reads as if written that way: "The CCA hands tokens out bit by bit and sets one price for everyone within each period."
yarn-dinkum.variety: Varied without leaning: "had a go", "four lots", "switched on", "kicked off", "done and dusted", "up for grabs", "down the track", "had a crack", "out of the blue"; "switched on" recurs.
yarn-dinkum.essence: Unmistakably the same FAQ, structure and code intact.

yarn-troppo.meaning: Facts are kept, but many asides add claims or gloss: "on the dot (well, near enough)", "one last hand-out" (the original never says last), "so nobody started lower than last time", "Anyone who reckons they can is dreamin'.", "That horse has bolted.", "Anyone who does is a shonk."
yarn-troppo.sense: Most terms fit: "Here's the good oil.", "not the whole box and dice", "shut up shop", "make life hard for snipers", "If it looks suss, it probably is.". "put its shoulder behind long-term on-chain liquidity" strains.
yarn-troppo.authenticity: The idiom is real, but stacked as tags: "Homework first.", "No ID, no go.", "Don't mix 'em up.", "Done.", "This bit matters.".
yarn-troppo.register: Well past level 3: nearly every section gets a quip or tag ("the sequel, if you like", "That horse has bolted.", "Anyone who does is a shonk."). No swearing.
yarn-troppo.tone: The FAQ's careful compliance voice turns flippant in places, worst on the risk line: "Nobody can tell ya. Anyone who reckons they can is dreamin'." Safety warnings get punchlines.
yarn-troppo.flow: Lively but choppy with fragments bolted after sentences: "So FOLD's now generally transferable. Done."
yarn-troppo.variety: Wide range, nothing leaned on: "good oil", "box and dice", "shut up shop", "done and dusted", "sussing out", "dreamin'", "horse has bolted", "nitty-gritty", "suss", "shonk".
yarn-troppo.essence: Recognisable as the FAQ, but its sober, compliance-first character is flattened by the running jokes.

unharnessed.meaning: Complete, with one overstatement: "cut down gas wars, stop sniping" turns mitigate into prevent. "from dodgy, unofficial sources" and "never, ever ask" are colour.
unharnessed.sense: Terms fit: "four lots", "kicked in", "locked in for long-term on-chain liquidity support", "done and dusted", "gas wars", "down the track", "dodgy".
unharnessed.authenticity: Natural mostly: "Auction 2 wrapped up not long before general FOLD transferability was switched on." One American form: "It's for folks who had a go".
unharnessed.register: Steady level 3 throughout, notices included: "Nothing in here counts as legal, tax, financial, investment, or other professional advice." No swearing.
unharnessed.tone: Mostly keeps the careful FAQ voice; the legal notices are made casual ("Nothing in here counts as"), softening their formality a little.
unharnessed.flow: Smooth on the whole: "The CCA hands out tokens bit by bit and uses the one price for everyone within each period."
unharnessed.variety: Good spread: "folks", "four lots", "kicked in", "locked in", "done and dusted", "gas wars", "Nope", "down the track", "had a go", "dodgy"; "kicked in" and "kicked off" both appear.
unharnessed.essence: Unmistakably the FAQ, structure and code intact.

dinkum-3.meaning: Complete: all figures, timestamps and links, CCA rules and notices kept; "Call `tgeTimestamp()` on the FOLD contract and you'll get back `1787148023`" is a fair recast.
dinkum-3.sense: Terms fit: "anyone who got in on the auction", "gave long-term on-chain liquidity a leg-up", "Bids that get up within a period", "all done and dusted", "before jumping in". "take the wind out of sniping" strains a little for mitigate.
dinkum-3.authenticity: Sounds like an Australian writing it: "Bids that get up within a period all clear at the same clearing price.", "Getting through verification didn't guarantee you eligibility or an allocation, mind."
dinkum-3.register: Right at level 3, notices left formal and the rest lightly retold: "leg-up", "get up", "done and dusted", "up for grabs", "Nah, nah.", "mind". No swearing.
dinkum-3.tone: The careful FAQ voice holds; warnings stay serious with only light emphasis: "Not ever."
dinkum-3.flow: Reads smoothly: "The CCA hands tokens out bit by bit, at the one price within each period."
dinkum-3.variety: Varied: "got in on", "leg-up", "locked in", "done and dusted", "get up", "take the wind out of", "up for grabs", "jumping in", "check out", "turn up out of the blue".
